content.title: About
content.content: The Double Cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of two small beef patties, two slices of cheese, a bun, lettuce, tomato, pickles, onion and sauce. It is prepared quickly and served hot.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Double Cheeseburger appeared on McDonald's menu in the 1970s as a heartier alternative.
Each small patty weighs about 45 g, so the total patty weight in the double version is roughly 90 g.
Two layers of cheese increase calcium content and give a richer flavor.
The burger is often served with fries and a soft drink as a "combo".
In some countries the double cheeseburger is adapted with local spices or sauces.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Beef patties provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese are rich in B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which aids oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and carbs quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A double cheeseburger contains about 500–600 kcal, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The levels of saturated fat and salt may contribute to higher cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten in the bun
items.content: Traditional buns contain wheat, which can be problematic for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is typically eaten with the hands, holding the bottom bun. Additional sauces, spices, or a gluten‑free bun can be used according to personal preference.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared double cheeseburgers should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 2 hours at 4 °C. For longer storage, freeze them and reheat in a microwave or on a grill before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Red Enchilada Sauce (4501) is a traditional Mexican sauce made from tomatoes, chilies, garlic and spices. It delivers a bright, mildly spicy flavor with smoky undertones and is used as a base for enchiladas, tacos and burritos.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce is named after the Mexican dish “enchilada,” where it is poured over the filling.
Classic recipes use dried ancho and chipotle chilies, giving it a distinctive smoky aroma.
Red sauce is often prepared in advance and can be kept in the refrigerator for several weeks.
In the United States it ranks among the top‑10 best‑selling sauces in the Mexican cuisine category.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike creamy sauces, red enchilada sauce contains virtually no saturated fat.

items.title: Source of capsaicin
items.content: Chilies add capsaicin, which may boost metabolism and have anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: The chili content can irritate the stomach of individuals sensitive to spicy foods.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or the spices used.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce can be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the sauce hot as a topping for enchiladas, casseroles, chili con carne, or use it as a dip for nachos and as a marinade for chicken or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks. After opening, it can be frozen in portions for up to 3 months. Discard if the smell or color changes.

pan-dulce-with-raisins-and-icing.title: Pan Dulce with Raisins and Icing

content.title: About
content.content: Pan Dulce is a traditional Mexican sweet bread, soft and fragrant, often enriched with raisins and topped with a sweet icing. The dough is made from wheat flour, eggs, butter, sugar and yeast, then raisins are folded in, adding a subtle fruity note. After baking, the loaf is glazed with a sugar icing, creating a pleasant contrast between the tender crumb and the crisp sweet crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pan Dulce originated in colonial Mexico, where Spanish pastry chefs adapted European recipes to local ingredients.
It is traditionally served during holidays, especially Day of the Dead and Christmas.
Raisins not only add sweetness but also retain moisture, keeping the bread soft and fresh longer.
Icing is usually made from powdered sugar, milk and vanilla, though some regions use honey or caramel syrup.
There are many regional variations: in Yucatán orange zest is added, while in Oaxaca pecans are common.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates and modest fat content provide a quick source of energy.

items.title: Rich in raisins
items.content: Raisins supply iron, potassium and antioxidants that support hemoglobin levels and cell protection.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough contributes B1, B2 and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Butter and milk in the recipe help strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Raisins and whole‑grain flour (when used) add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The icing and raisins make the product sweet, which can be problematic for people with diabetes or those limiting sugar.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, so it is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of butter, sugar and raisins, Pan Dulce is relatively high in calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Dried fruit sensitivity
items.content: Raisins may cause increased gas in individuals with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pan Dulce is enjoyed as a dessert with tea or coffee, sliced and lightly warmed. It pairs well with hot chocolate, fruit sauces, or cream cheese spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate (up to 1 week) or freeze (up to 2 months). Allow the bread to come to room temperature before serving.

peas-and-corn-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Peas and corn, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Peas and corn are two popular vegetables often combined in cooking. When prepared without added fat they retain their natural flavor, texture, and most of their nutrients. Peas are rich in protein and fiber, while corn provides carbohydrates and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 10,000 years.
Corn was domesticated in Mesoamerica about 9,000 years ago.
The pea‑corn combination appears in many traditional dishes, such as American corn‑and‑pea salad or Indian matar makai.
Cooking without fat preserves more vitamin C, which is heat‑ and fat‑sensitive.
Together peas and corn create a more complete amino‑acid profile than either alone.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, making them a solid meat alternative for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Both vegetables supply soluble and insoluble fiber that supports digestive health and blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn supplies thiamine (B1) and folate (B9), while peas are a good source of vitamin B6, important for amino‑acid metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Peas contain iron, magnesium and zinc; corn contributes potassium and phosphorus, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Preparing without added fat keeps the dish light and suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to legumes (peas) or to corn.

items.title: Anti‑nutrient content
items.content: Peas contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; cooking reduces its level.

items.title: Corn’s glycemic index
items.content: Corn has a relatively high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peas and corn can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, or stews. They reheat well in the microwave or steam. For extra flavor, toss with fresh herbs, lemon juice, or a pinch of spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions; reheat using a microwave or steam to retain texture.
